hypothesis: Cached assignment policies reduce returning-motif churn under some regimes but may increase matching search work. Compare both churn and augmenting-path search calls under newly disjoint cohorts to determine if quorum2 is a multiobjective Pareto improvement.
freeze: All comparison arms, four geometry families, budgets and strict Pareto classification frozen before the original first use; no model/policy retraining.
population: Exactly seven active of sixteen motif identities/cells, maximum nine inactive cached assignments, 8 episodes and radius2 matching, same Y036 deterministic neighborhood/home generator and exhaustive Hall oracle.
metrics: For all heldout seeds and four regimes, total matching recursion calls (only within the core matcher; no fabricated wall time), returning-key placement churn, legal preferences, cache writes, cache occupancy and max-matching cardinality. Assess both aggregate and worst-regime cost.
primary: PARETO_QUORUM2 if across ALL four regimes quorum2 has churn<=full AND recursive_calls<=full, with at least one strict improvement, while slow-drift quorum2 preserves >=70% of full saving vs sham. TRADEOFF if any regime improves BOTH churn and calls but strong condition fails; NOT_PARETO otherwise. Preserve per-regime regressions and negative outcomes.
controls: All policies see only observed assignments and present graph
Identical cache writes/keys and seven exact legal matches per episode verified with independent Hall
Call counter must be the existing matcher return, not an additional search budget
One source-frozen original artifact plus full pytest; no retries, accepted-ref or production mutations
claim_limit: Synthetic multiobjective matcher cost and retention analysis, not model-call compute or learned semantics.
